edition.name: Duncker & Schneidewin, Göttingen 1859 (Refutatio omnium haeresium), First1KGreek/Perseus TEI tlg2115.tlg060 (local copy)
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ τῆς γενεαλογίας αὐτῶν τὴν διαδοχὴν ἐπεδείξαμεν, δοκεῖ λοιπὸν καὶ τῶν δογμάτων τὴν κακοδιδασκαλίαν ἐκθέσθαι, [καὶ] πρότερον τὰ Ἡρακλείτῳ τῷ σκοτεινῷ δόξαντα παραθεμένους, ἔπειτα καὶ τὰ τούτων μέρη Ἡρακλείτεια ὄντα φανερῶσαι, ἃ τυχόντες οἱ νῦν προστάται τῆς αἱρέσεως οὐκ ἴσασιν ὄντα τοῦ σκοτεινοῦ, νομίζοντες εἶναι Χριστοῦ. Οἷς εἰ ἐνέτυχον, κἂν οὕτω δυσωπηθέντες παύσονται τῆς ἀθέου δυσφημίας. Ἀλλ᾿ εἰ καὶ πρότερον ἔκκειται ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν ἐν τοῖς Φιλοσοφουμένοις ἡ δόξα Ἡρακλείτου, ἀλλά γε δοκεῖ προσαναπαραχθῆναι καὶ νῦν, ὅπως διὰ τοῦ ἐγγίονος ἐλέγχου φανερῶς διδαχθῶσιν οἱ τούτου νομίζοντες Χριστοῦ εἷναι μαθητάς, οὐκ ὄντας, ἀλλὰ τοῦ σκοτεινοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: But since we have shown the succession of their genealogy, it seems that next also the bad teaching of their doctrines should be set forth, and first having set forth the things that seemed to Heraclitus the dark one, then also the parts of these things being Heraclitean should be made clear, which the current leaders of the heresy, having chanced upon, do not know are of the dark one, thinking they are of Christ. To whom if they should encounter, even being persuaded in this way they will stop the atheistic blasphemy. But if also before the opinion of Heraclitus has been set forth by us in the Philosophumena, nevertheless it seems to be drawn near also now, so that through the near proof they may be taught clearly, those thinking they are disciples of Christ, not being, but of the dark one.
pass_b_english: Having demonstrated the succession of their genealogy, we must now also set forth the false teaching of their doctrines. First we will present the opinions of Heraclitus the Obscure, and then we will make clear which parts of this heresy are Heraclitean. The current leaders of the heresy stumbled upon these ideas but do not realize they come from the Obscure One; they think they come from Christ. If they encountered Heraclitus himself, even then they would be convinced and would stop their atheistic blasphemy. Although we have already expounded Heraclitus's system in the Philosophumena, we must bring it forward again now, so that through this closer refutation those who suppose they are disciples of Christ may be taught plainly that they are not his followers but followers of the Obscure One.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A is a faithful literal translation, and Pass B is a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances of agency, negation, and doctrine. The epithet 'σκοτεινῷ' is consistently rendered as 'the dark one' or 'the Obscure One'. The reference to 'Philosophumena' (Φιλοσοφουμένοις) is correctly handled.
